findings.title: Auto-update chain executes upstream-controlled code on every fork
findings.description: Daily workflow runs repo copy of scripts/sync-upstream.mjs, which is itself replaced by upstream on each sync (only .github/workflows/ is protected). Compromised upstream main gets code execution in every fork runner (contents:write GITHUB_TOKEN) within 24h, and its git push triggers Cloudflare Workers Build running npm ci + prebuild with the deployer's Cloudflare API token and remote D1 write.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker compromises upstream TedLin1993/all-set-tw main -> injects payload into scripts/sync-upstream.mjs or package.json/postinstall -> every deployed fork syncs within 24h -> fork runner executes payload with contents:write token; pushed merge triggers Cloudflare build executing arbitrary code with deployer Cloudflare credentials + D1 access to their financial data.
findings.impact: Supply-chain RCE across all deployed forks; access to each deployer's Cloudflare account token and encrypted financial DB.
findings.recommendation: This is a deliberate auto-update tradeoff; accept with mitigations. SHA-pin actions/checkout and setup-node; add persist-credentials:false to the sync checkout; pin the bootstrap curl download to a commit SHA + checksum; consider signing releases or requiring a tag rather than tracking mutable main.

findings.title: User-supplied regex run per-transaction with no timeout (ReDoS self-DoS)
findings.description: new RegExp(rule.pattern, 'i').test(text) compiles a user-stored classification rule pattern (max 300 chars) and runs it against every transaction on every /api/bank-transactions and /api/activity read. try/catch only swallows syntax errors, not catastrophic backtracking.
findings.exploit_scenario: Authenticated user saves a regex rule like (a+)+$ -> every subsequent transaction listing re-evaluates it per row -> Worker hits CPU limit and requests fail persistently until the rule is deleted.
findings.impact: Persistent self-inflicted DoS of the read path. Not reachable in demo mode (write blocked by demoReadOnlyMiddleware). Single-tenant per deployment, so blast radius is the owner only.
findings.recommendation: Add a length+complexity guard, run the regex with a RE2-style linear engine, or cap total match time. Cheapest: reject patterns with nested quantifiers, keep the 300-char cap low.

findings.title: 7 npm advisories (hono x2, ip-address x3 high) — none reachable in runtime path
findings.description: npm audit: 2 moderate (hono Proxy Helper header leak, Language middleware ReDoS), 5 high (ip-address SSRF misclassification x3, others). hono Proxy Helper and languageDetector are NOT imported anywhere. ip-address is transitive via @puppeteer/browsers > proxy-agent > socks-proxy-agent, used only for local browser download/launch, not the Workers BROWSER binding runtime path.
findings.exploit_scenario: No reachable path found. Advisories apply to code the app never executes at runtime.
findings.impact: Low practical risk today; hygiene debt. npm audit fix resolves both without breaking changes.
findings.recommendation: Run npm audit fix to update hono (4.12.26 -> patched) and bump the puppeteer chain. Re-run audit in CI as a gate.

findings.title: Connector error strings persisted unredacted, served on GET /api/sync-jobs (readable in demo mode)
findings.description: safeErrorMessage only truncates to 300 chars; it does NOT redact URLs/tokens/cookies (unlike sanitizeErrorDiagnostic used for logs). Its output is stored as last_error and returned by GET /api/sync-jobs, which is readable by unauthenticated visitors in demo mode. Upstream bank error text (e.g. obank statusDesc interpolated verbatim) can land there.
findings.exploit_scenario: Bank returns an error containing a URL/token in statusDesc -> stored verbatim in last_error -> anyone hitting the demo deployment's GET /api/sync-jobs reads it.
findings.impact: Potential low-volume disclosure of upstream-embedded values in demo deployments. No app secret confirmed leaked.
findings.recommendation: Apply sanitizeErrorDiagnostic's redaction inside safeErrorMessage so stored/served messages are scrubbed.

findings.title: VAPID private key written to shared temp dir in plaintext during deploy
findings.description: Private key written to a mkdtemp (0700) file with mode 0o600, removed in finally{}. finally does not run on SIGINT/SIGKILL/crash (no signal handler, unlike dev-worker.mjs), leaving the key in os.tmpdir(). When source secrets file is dotenv, its entire contents are copied into the temp file.
findings.exploit_scenario: Deploy interrupted with SIGKILL -> plaintext VAPID private key (and any other dotenv secrets) remain in os.tmpdir() until manually cleared; another local user reads them.
findings.impact: Local-only, requires deploy interruption + shared host. Push notifications can be spoofed if key leaks.
findings.recommendation: Add SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler; pass secrets to wrangler via stdin instead of a temp file.

findings.title: Actions tag-pinned not SHA-pinned; ci.yml has no permissions block
findings.description: actions/checkout@v4 and setup-node@v4 use mutable tags in both workflows. ci.yml declares no permissions:, inheriting default GITHUB_TOKEN scope while running npm ci (executes dependency lifecycle scripts).
findings.exploit_scenario: Tag re-point or default-write token abused if a dependency postinstall is malicious during npm ci.
findings.impact: Standard CI hardening gap. Elevated for the contents:write sync job.
findings.recommendation: SHA-pin all actions; add permissions: contents: read to ci.yml.

findings.title: E.SUN session cookie jar replayed to manual-redirect targets without origin check
findings.description: Manual redirect following (up to 5 hops) sets the full E.SUN cookie jar on each hop with no same-origin guard, unlike Taishin's domain allowlist. Attacker must control the bank's Location response, so this is defense-in-depth only.
findings.exploit_scenario: If E.SUN infra returned an off-origin Location, session cookies would be sent to that host.
findings.recommendation: Add a same-origin check before replaying cookies on redirect, matching the Taishin allowlist pattern.
